text: Which you can adjust. It doesn't say that. It is a proprietary solution of the manufacturer that produces Wi-Fi cards. So every manufacturer has got its own algorithm that allows you allows the the Wi-Fi card to adjust to the propagation conditions. However, there are two basic ways to do that. Okay. So general principles that are used by the manufacturers. Either your receiver estimates the SNR and sends back to the transmitter the value of SNR. And then the transmitter checks this value. If the SNR experienced by the receiver is high, it means good channel, then the transmitter increases the data rate. If instead the SNR is low, then the transmitter decreases the data rate. The other possibility is that you exploit the history of successful packets. So for each packet, remember that in Wi-Fi when the transmitter transmits successfully, it receives an acknowledgement, right? So the transmitter can records the acknowledgments for each transmission. If it sees that is transmission is actually on average usually successful, then it can try and increase the data rate. If instead it records failures, it decreases the data rate.
